Chapter 7: The Weight of Injustice and the Longing for Fairness
Have you ever felt that heaviness—when something just isn’t fair? It’s like the world tilts a little, and suddenly, it seems like the rules don’t quite apply the same way to everyone. That weight is hard to put into words, but you’ll notice it in the little things—the small slights, the big exclusions, the doors that never quite open, and the voices that just aren’t heard.
Picture this: someone at work who does everything right. They show up early, stay late, lend a hand whenever they can. But when it comes time for a promotion, they’re passed over—not because of their work, but because of something they can’t change. Maybe it’s their gender, their background, or even their accent. The disappointment stings, of course, but what really sticks is feeling invisible, like no one truly sees who they are or what they can do.
Most people don’t realize just how deep the cost of injustice runs. It isn’t only about a missed opportunity or lost income. It’s about how hope slowly fades, and how dreams start to shrink—forced to fit into the smaller spaces that are left. Over time, people adapt. They expect less, ask for less, and even start to settle for less.
But here’s the thing—the longing for fairness never really disappears. It finds its way into those quiet acts of resistance. Maybe it’s someone speaking up during a meeting, or refusing to laugh at a cruel joke, or deciding to help a coworker who’s been left out. These moments might seem small, but honestly, they’re where change begins.
What becomes clear is that justice isn’t just about laws or official policies—it's woven into the everyday choices we all make. Will we include or exclude? Listen or ignore? Lift someone up, or hold them back? When fairness becomes part of daily life, everyone feels the difference. Trust grows, new possibilities open up, and the world just feels a bit more welcoming.
